title: VOID — Integration Stack & Infrastructure
status: Research-backed recommendation; not a validated build
scope: Desktop studio first; macOS, Windows and Linux qualification. No repository changes.
assumptions: Tauri/Rust platform with C++ permitted is accepted direction.
Proprietary or mixed distribution remains possible; open-sourcing VOID has not been approved.
The initial release remains local-first; cloud inference and collaboration are optional.

libraries.name: Tauri + Rust
libraries.proof: Established desktop framework; not evidence that VOID audio is already qualified.
libraries.docs: Strong: architecture, capabilities, packaging, updater and test guides.
libraries.reuse: Desktop lifecycle, menus, file dialogs, windows, scoped native commands and updates.
libraries.custom: Keep the shell small. Rust supervises workers and owns app services. React/TS remains a bounded presentation layer.
libraries.risk: System WebViews vary by OS. Native plugin windows and GPU output need platform tests; Rust does not eliminate WebView leaks.

libraries.name: Tracktion Engine
libraries.proof: Direct production evidence: Waveform Free is built on this engine.
libraries.docs: Good examples/tutorials/tests; some API documentation remains incomplete.
libraries.reuse: Use its musical Edit model rather than writing another sequencer. See the capability boundary below.
libraries.custom: Build a narrow command adapter and stable object-ID mapping. Preserve engine save/load and musical undo behind the adapter.
libraries.risk: Not a complete studio UI. Confirm licensed major version, supported JUCE revision and native-window integration before committing.

libraries.name: JUCE
libraries.proof: Established audio framework; underpins the selected engine and shipping plugins.
libraries.docs: Strong API reference, examples, tutorials and release notes.
libraries.reuse: Audio/MIDI devices, DSP primitives, plugin hosting, native plugin windows, OSC and platform glue.
libraries.custom: One device/transport owner in the C++ worker. Reuse hosted formats before adding separate hosts.
libraries.risk: A plugin creation format is not necessarily a host format. Qualify AU/VST3 explicitly; do not promise AAX hosting. Pin the engine-compatible JUCE pair.

libraries.name: Ardour / libardour
libraries.license: Copyleft; confirm selected source licence and dependencies
libraries.proof: Shipping professional DAW with a real backend.
libraries.docs: Large developer/API documentation; headless example is described as a demonstration.
libraries.reuse: A substantial audio/session foundation when a copyleft product or full application fork is intentional.
libraries.custom: Adapt application-shaped APIs, session/UI coupling and integration contracts.
libraries.risk: Not the lowest-friction embeddable SDK. More fork/architecture responsibility than the default path.

libraries.name: Carla
libraries.proof: Shipping multi-format plugin host.
libraries.docs: README/build instructions and examples; feature maturity is mixed.
libraries.reuse: Consider for an explicitly compatible copyleft host architecture or as a reference.
libraries.custom: Avoid installing a second competing host beside Tracktion without a defined gap.
libraries.risk: Its README identifies plugin bridging/transport work as experimental. Do not sell it as a turnkey crash-isolation subsystem.

libraries.name: Cockos WDL
libraries.license: Permissive notices per component; review exact files
libraries.proof: Cockos states that its own applications use WDL.
libraries.docs: Source-oriented utility library rather than a complete DAW SDK.
libraries.reuse: Use a narrowly justified utility or DSP component when the selected engine lacks it.
libraries.custom: Wrap only the module needed; retain notice and regression fixtures.
libraries.risk: WDL is not the REAPER engine and does not supply REAPER-level session behavior.

libraries.name: Signalsmith Stretch
libraries.proof: Listed in current Tracktion dependencies; also used by Audiomentations.
libraries.docs: Useful API-level timing, latency and formant documentation.
libraries.reuse: Pitch/time processing; prefer the version already integrated by the engine.
libraries.custom: Map warp edits and preserve input/output latency and render tails; add musical quality fixtures.
libraries.risk: Not a Flex Pitch editor. The author warns that modest time ratios sound best; extreme ratios need listening tests.

libraries.name: Rubber Band / SoundTouch
libraries.license: Rubber Band: GPL-2.0+ / commercial. SoundTouch: LGPL-2.1.
libraries.proof: Long-lived specialist libraries; Rubber Band has a published release history.
libraries.docs: Dedicated API and licensing guides.
libraries.reuse: Alternative stretch/pitch backend when the selected default fails quality or performance tests.
libraries.custom: Benchmark the same transient, voice and polyphonic fixtures, then select one backend per use case.
libraries.risk: Do not add every stretcher. Check linkage, latency and additional licensing; a library swap does not create an editing workflow.

libraries.name: Tracktion stock instruments and effects
libraries.proof: Shipped engine features include 4OSC, a simple sampler and basic effects.
libraries.docs: Engine feature reference and example projects.
libraries.reuse: Bootstrap playable synth, one-shots, basic EQ/dynamics/delay and routing without a new DSP framework.
libraries.custom: Build instrument controls, curated presets, browser metadata and MIDI/automation mappings.
libraries.risk: This is a starter palette, not an Alchemy/Kontakt-scale sound library. Sound content must be original or licensed separately.

libraries.name: FluidSynth
libraries.license: LGPL-2.1 family; verify exact distribution build
libraries.proof: Official site lists integrations including LMMS, MusE and Qsynth.
libraries.docs: API/development documentation and maintained source repository.
libraries.reuse: SoundFont instrument playback for a reusable initial acoustic/general instrument palette.
libraries.custom: Drive its synthesis from the engine. Do not create a competing FluidSynth device driver or enable an unnecessary command server.
libraries.risk: SF2 playback is not full SFZ/Kontakt multisampling. Approve every sound bank separately and bound voices/sample memory.

libraries.name: Airwindows Consolidated library
libraries.license: MIT for the specified core library; wrappers bring separate dependencies
libraries.proof: Shipping Airwindows Consolidated DAW and VCV Rack products.
libraries.docs: Good user manuals; developer registry documentation is explicitly unfinished.
libraries.reuse: The airwin-registry CMake target exposes reusable effect implementations.
libraries.custom: Ship a tested curated subset with VOID controls, presets, loudness matching and parameter automation.
libraries.risk: Do not pull whole wrapper builds indiscriminately. Validate CPU, gain, denormals, sample-rate behavior and tails per effect.

libraries.name: sfizz
libraries.license: BSD-2-Clause core in reviewed source; audit transitive components
libraries.proof: Shipped SFZ library/plugins, but original repository archived on 21 June 2026.
libraries.docs: API/opcode material exists; forward maintenance is unresolved.
libraries.reuse: Potential advanced SFZ engine only after identifying a credible maintained successor or funding a fork.
libraries.custom: A successor/fork needs an owner, security patch channel, reproducible builds and regression corpus.
libraries.risk: Not the default for a maintenance-first project. An old release being usable is not proof of future maintenance.

libraries.name: HISE
libraries.proof: Instrument-building toolkit with an actual export workflow and player ecosystem.
libraries.docs: Extensive developer documentation and community support.
libraries.reuse: Alternative for sophisticated sample-based instruments and effects.
libraries.custom: Prefer authoring a native instrument plugin hosted by VOID before trying to embed the whole authoring environment.
libraries.risk: Large toolkit overlap; additional commercial agreement for a closed distribution. Benchmark memory and disk-streaming requirements.

libraries.name: Surge XT
libraries.proof: Shipping synthesizer with commercial-product ancestry and regular platform releases.
libraries.docs: Developer build/test guides and user documentation.
libraries.reuse: Support user-installed Surge XT as a first-class compatibility target.
libraries.custom: Persist plugin state and expose macros/automation through the standard host path.
libraries.risk: Do not copy its GPL source into a proprietary engine. Any bundling or derivative needs a distribution/licence review.

libraries.name: libebur128
libraries.proof: Mature specialist C library with loudness/true-peak conformance tests; downstream app usage not independently established here.
libraries.docs: Small documented C API and example/test programs.
libraries.reuse: Loudness, loudness range and true-peak measurement.
libraries.custom: Display metering, target-based export checks and reference comparison; allocate state outside the audio callback.
libraries.risk: Meters are not automatic mastering. Conformance tests and channel-layout validation remain release gates.

libraries.name: libsndfile
libraries.proof: Long-lived native audio-file library with team stewardship and fuzz/regression infrastructure.
libraries.docs: Detailed build/format documentation and examples.
libraries.reuse: Add a file format only when JUCE/engine support does not cover the requirement.
libraries.custom: Use controlled import workers and normalized internal assets.
libraries.risk: Do not maintain duplicate decoder paths for the same format without need; fuzz malformed media and cap decoded sizes.

libraries.name: Steinberg VST 3 SDK
libraries.proof: Vendor SDK and developer portal for the VST3 plugin ecosystem.
libraries.docs: Strong interface docs, examples and validation tools.
libraries.reuse: Native third-party instrument/effect interoperability via JUCE.
libraries.custom: Build scan cache, quarantine, compatible plugin versions, missing-plugin recovery and state restoration.
libraries.risk: Current MIT licensing does not grant rights to VST2 or third-party plugins. Use the licence of the exact bundled SDK revision.

libraries.name: CLAP
libraries.proof: Published audio plugin standard with ecosystem implementations.
libraries.docs: API header specification, extensions and support material.
libraries.reuse: Add CLAP when the required plugin audience justifies another host adapter.
libraries.custom: Explicitly implement and test host extensions, state, events and plugin windows.
libraries.risk: Do not infer CLAP host support merely because an unrelated JUCE project exports CLAP plugins.

libraries.name: Ableton Link
libraries.proof: Ableton-maintained synchronization SDK.
libraries.docs: Conceptual clock docs, example apps and a behavior test plan.
libraries.reuse: Cross-device beat/tempo/phase synchronization for performance.
libraries.custom: Translate device latency/clock snapshots and apply user-approved tempo ownership rules.
libraries.risk: Network sync is not the internal sample clock. Obtain appropriate rights and qualify the exact feature set/version.

libraries.name: DAWproject
libraries.proof: Official repository lists Bitwig, Studio One, Cubase and other adopters.
libraries.docs: Schema, examples and documented object model.
libraries.reuse: Cross-DAW arrangement/interchange path alongside audio stems and Standard MIDI Files.
libraries.custom: Map a declared subset and produce a loss report for unsupported instruments, automation or routing.
libraries.risk: Not a universal .logicx importer. Plugin availability/state and DAW-specific features can still prevent exact round trips.

libraries.name: SQLite
libraries.proof: Widely deployed in operating systems, browsers and applications.
libraries.docs: Extensive documentation, backup API and WAL details.
libraries.reuse: Local project metadata, asset index, job history, provenance and searchable preferences.
libraries.custom: Rust coordinates durable checkpoints with the engine snapshot; media remains immutable files, not large DB blobs.
libraries.risk: Use a patched supported build; do not cloud-sync a live WAL database or put it on a network filesystem. SQLite alone does not atomically commit external media.

libraries.name: FlatBuffers
libraries.proof: Established cross-language serialization project.
libraries.docs: Rust/C++ examples and schema evolution guidance.
libraries.reuse: Versioned control messages and compact read-only state/telemetry snapshots.
libraries.custom: Define protocol negotiation, bounded frames, command IDs, validation and explicit backpressure.
libraries.risk: Not a transport, scheduler or sandbox. No serialization or WebView IPC inside the audio callback; use native preallocated buffers where PCM must cross processes.

libraries.name: Tokio and a small Rust service layer
libraries.license: Tokio: MIT; review each additional crate separately
libraries.proof: Tokio documents production adoption outside audio.
libraries.docs: Strong async/network/process documentation.
libraries.reuse: Worker supervision, downloads, local IPC and cancellable background jobs.
libraries.custom: Use bounded queues; isolate database/disk work and CPU-heavy tasks. Add serialization/logging/HTTP crates only as needed.
libraries.risk: Tokio is not the real-time audio scheduler. An async task can still block, allocate or monopolize CPU.

libraries.name: ONNX Runtime
libraries.proof: Direct production evidence: Windows, Office, Azure Cognitive Services and Bing.
libraries.docs: Strong APIs, provider matrix and optimization guides.
libraries.reuse: Portable inference for compact qualified analysis/transcription/gesture models.
libraries.custom: Select execution provider per hardware and model; package a CPU fallback when practical. Audit and disable optional runtime diagnostic collection by default; verify the packaged build has no unexpected telemetry.
libraries.risk: Provider support varies. A proven runtime does not validate a particular music model or its exported graph.

libraries.name: llama.cpp
libraries.license: MIT runtime; chosen weights independently licensed
libraries.proof: Established local-inference runtime; not a production musical autocomplete system by itself.
libraries.docs: Build/backend docs, server tools and structured-output grammar support.
libraries.reuse: Small local language-model inference for intent interpretation and symbolic proposals.
libraries.custom: Typed tools, project context selection, constrained MIDI proposals, caching and cancellation remain VOID responsibilities.
libraries.risk: No model runs on the audio thread. Pin runtime/model revisions; enforce output validation instead of trusting generated JSON.

libraries.name: Demucs, author-maintained fork
libraries.license: MIT code; audit downloaded model artifacts
libraries.proof: Author lists adoption by UVR, Audiostrip, MVSep and related tools.
libraries.docs: Usable CLI/Python documentation; fork explicitly warns of slow maintenance and no expected new features.
libraries.reuse: Stem separation as a replaceable offline worker.
libraries.custom: Package a tested runtime/model bundle and retain output alignment, source hash and job provenance.
libraries.risk: Meta original is archived. Even the author fork needs an owned patch strategy; do not promote it to an unmaintained hard core dependency.

libraries.name: Spotify Basic Pitch
libraries.proof: Publisher-backed audio-to-MIDI project with a working model/demo; not proof of perfect production transcription.
libraries.docs: Installation, inference and limitation guidance.
libraries.reuse: Assist conversion of recorded musical audio into editable note candidates.
libraries.custom: Provide correction UI, confidence and original-audio A/B. Prefer isolated sources when possible.
libraries.risk: Not a next-note autocomplete model, and not a substitute for stem separation. Validate polyphony, bends and note timing.

libraries.name: music21, code-only/no-corpus build
libraries.license: BSD-3-Clause code; corpus has separate restrictions
libraries.proof: Long-established computational musicology toolkit.
libraries.docs: Extensive user guide and reference documentation.
libraries.reuse: Offline chord/key analysis, symbolic-music utilities and proposal validation helpers.
libraries.custom: Build fast native constraints only where interaction latency requires them; run richer analysis in a worker.
libraries.risk: Do not redistribute or train from its bundled corpus automatically. Current Python requirements must match the packaged worker.

libraries.name: ACE-Step 1.5
libraries.license: MIT project; approve exact model weight licences and provenance
libraries.proof: Emerging music-generation project, not established DAW infrastructure.
libraries.docs: Project docs and author benchmarks; VOID suitability remains unmeasured.
libraries.reuse: Candidate for prompt-conditioned generated audio assets.
libraries.custom: Asynchronous job adapter, audition, alignment, regeneration, acceptance and cache lifecycle.
libraries.risk: Do not repeat author speed/VRAM claims as VOID guarantees. Missing model/network must never disable ordinary composition.

libraries.name: Diffusers + approved visual model
libraries.license: Apache-2.0 library; FLUX.1-schnell card specifies Apache-2.0 weights
libraries.proof: Diffusers lists adoption by InvokeAI and Apple-related tooling.
libraries.docs: Strong pipeline and optimization docs.
libraries.reuse: Generate images or pre-rendered visual assets in a pinned worker; FLUX.1-schnell is one licence-clear evaluation example, not a claim of best current quality.
libraries.custom: Add asset provenance, resolution limits, cancellation, seed/config capture and audition before publishing to a project.
libraries.risk: Weight/runtime/content rights are separate. Video models require their own selection and hardware budget; no instant live generation promise.

libraries.name: Essentia
libraries.license: AGPL/commercial code path; models have separate non-commercial/proprietary terms
libraries.proof: Specialist music-analysis framework; do not assume its model terms match its code.
libraries.docs: Detailed algorithm and licensing documentation.
libraries.reuse: Broad music feature analysis if a commercial/compatible licence is justified.
libraries.custom: Compile only required algorithms and clear every selected model/dependency.
libraries.risk: Not a blanket permissive add-on. Prefer smaller approved features until its breadth is needed.

libraries.name: MediaPipe Hand Landmarker
libraries.license: Project/asset licence review required for the exact SDK and task bundle
libraries.proof: Google-maintained perception SDK; musical gesture UX is not supplied.
libraries.docs: Task guides, callbacks and image/video/live running modes.
libraries.reuse: Camera landmarks and tracking rather than custom computer vision training.
libraries.custom: Native or isolated worker integration, confidence filtering, calibration, clutch, smoothing and note-off safety. Touch/trackpad/MIDI come first.
libraries.risk: Dropped frames/occlusion must not leave stuck notes. Camera consent, local processing and timestamp mapping are product work.

libraries.name: wgpu
libraries.proof: Official project identifies usage in Firefox, Servo and Deno.
libraries.docs: Backend/API docs; regular breaking-release cadence requires pinning.
libraries.reuse: Native cross-platform GPU rendering foundation.
libraries.custom: VOID still supplies layers, scene graph, visual automation, shader controls and output scheduling. Start with a separate native output window.
libraries.risk: Not an off-the-shelf visual editor. No automatic zero-copy embedding into a Tauri WebView or projectM OpenGL context.

libraries.name: projectM
libraries.license: LGPL-2.1 core; presets and frontends separately licensed
libraries.proof: Shipped integration: Kodi; original ecosystem also includes media-player use.
libraries.docs: Core API/build docs; repository warns some frontends are outdated/development previews.
libraries.reuse: Optional MilkDrop-style audio-reactive preset renderer with existing visual behavior.
libraries.custom: Isolate an OpenGL-based output path and distribute only approved presets. Feed copied bounded analysis/PCM data, not blocking audio calls.
libraries.risk: Do not rebuild its shader parser, but do not force it into wgpu as if APIs matched. A transition plan is needed for compositing/export.

libraries.name: FFmpeg
libraries.license: Build-dependent: LGPL default paths; optional GPL/nonfree components change obligations
libraries.proof: Long-established native media infrastructure.
libraries.docs: Extensive tool/library docs and an explicit redistribution checklist.
libraries.reuse: Decode/transcode audiovisual assets and produce final synchronized exports.
libraries.custom: Versioned controlled worker with input/output manifests and bounded resources.
libraries.risk: Approve a specific codec/build matrix, not a random binary download. Patents and third-party codec terms need separate review. Never run codecs in the audio callback.

libraries.name: Verovio
libraries.proof: Shipping online editor/viewer and supported native/web bindings.
libraries.docs: Reference book, integration examples and C++ API.
libraries.reuse: Score engraving from MEI and supported import formats such as MusicXML.
libraries.custom: Map notes to notation objects, interactive edits, selections and layout preferences.
libraries.risk: Engraving is not a complete score editor; it does not supply Logic-style notation workflow for free.

libraries.name: Open Lighting Architecture
libraries.license: Mixed components; LGPL client and GPL-related code require review
libraries.proof: Established lighting-protocol framework with hardware adapters.
libraries.docs: API/tutorial/build documentation.
libraries.reuse: DMX/sACN and equipment transport through its daemon/client architecture.
libraries.custom: VOID creates cue rules, approved fixture profiles, rehearsal, output permission and a manual blackout path.
libraries.risk: Windows support is partial. Do not make stage control a dependency of the studio or let generated instructions directly actuate fixtures.

libraries.name: Wasmtime
libraries.proof: Established Bytecode Alliance WebAssembly runtime.
libraries.docs: Runtime/security/API documentation.
libraries.reuse: A future restricted environment for custom procedural/generative modules.
libraries.custom: Design an explicit capability API with resource limits, cancellation and no ambient filesystem/network rights.
libraries.risk: Runtime sandboxing is not automatic real-time suitability; untrusted modules stay outside the critical playback path until proven.

libraries.name: pluginval + vendor validators
libraries.license: pluginval GPL-3.0 as a separate test tool; vendor tools separately reviewed
libraries.proof: Purpose-built audio-plugin validation tool with headless operation.
libraries.docs: CLI examples and test documentation.
libraries.reuse: Exercise fixtures and embedded/generated plugins in CI; add VST3 SDK validators and platform AU tools.
libraries.custom: Host integration tests, crash/restore tests and hardware loopback are still needed.
libraries.risk: Do not link GPL test-tool code into an unrelated proprietary runtime. Plugin validation does not certify the host or every third-party plugin.

libraries.name: WebdriverIO Tauri service
libraries.license: Inspect service/plugin licences at the pinned revision
libraries.proof: Official current Tauri-recommended E2E integration.
libraries.docs: Current setup guides explain Windows/Linux/macOS and embedded driver mode.
libraries.reuse: Reusable cross-platform desktop E2E tests rather than a custom UI automation framework.
libraries.custom: Use test-only embedded automation plugins and command hooks; remove them from production builds.
libraries.risk: Direct tauri-driver still lacks macOS WKWebView support, but the current embedded service supports macOS. Native plugin/editor/device tests need additional coverage.

libraries.name: Tauri updater + native CI packaging
libraries.license: Tauri plugin terms plus OS signing/distribution terms
libraries.proof: Documented cross-platform installer and update path.
libraries.docs: Strong signing/static manifest configuration examples.
libraries.reuse: Signed update artifacts and staged release channels. A static HTTPS manifest can serve initial updates.
libraries.custom: Protect signing keys, build nested workers, notarize/sign platform artifacts, retain matching sources/notices and test update interruption.
libraries.risk: Updater signature does not replace OS code signing. Never install/restart during recording or a live performance.
